purpose: Product and dependency update backlog snapshot after the provider-neutral code-intelligence integration.

products.notes: Updated to v0.2.67 after reviewing v0.2.63 through v0.2.67. The refresh brings machine-readable MCP readiness/contract envelopes, supplier-diff analysis, parser recovery, SDBL, diagnostics, type-inference, metadata module-path and Linux compatibility fixes; v0.2.67 also adds multi-root indexing, root_id, global unresolved-name search and an explicit cache directory. Unica continues to consume only its existing typed graph, diagnostics and single-root search boundaries over the hidden stdio provider. HTTP transport, ignored_authors, supplier-diff scope, multi-root/root_id/cache controls and other upstream commands are not exposed as unica.* tools; dependency-aware CFE topology remains outside this update.

Updated together with rlm-bsl-index to unmodified upstream v1.29.1. The reviewed delta keeps helper and index schema contracts compatible while adding process-isolated persistent sandboxes, hard execution timeout, session teardown fixes, and the Linux spawn-broker hotfix. Unica uses only rlm_start/rlm_execute/rlm_end with fixed helper templates; raw RLM helper guidance remains hidden from skills.

v1.29.1 keeps index schema and BUILDER_VERSION 14, so existing worktree-local indexes remain reusable without destructive migration. Contract gates verify the supported build/info/update CLI lifecycle and generated package launchers; Unica no longer reads or validates private SQLite tables.
Updated tools.lock.json to v0.5.1 after reviewing the version command and partial-load/build changes; Unica MCP contract remains typed and unchanged.
Source pin is current; local interpreter may still have 6.1.0 until test requirements are installed.
Applied compatible lock-only updates: cc 1.2.64 -> 1.2.65, log 0.4.32 -> 0.4.33, quote 1.0.45 -> 1.0.46, and rustls 0.23.40 -> 0.23.41; direct major updates stay out of this batch.
serde_yaml is deprecated, but replacing the YAML parser is a direct dependency migration rather than a lock refresh; defer to a separate focused PR with v8project.yaml fixture coverage.
ureq 3.3.0 requires Rust 1.85. The repo does not currently publish an MSRV, so the dependency stays on ureq 2.12.1 until Rust 1.85 support is an explicit release-policy decision.
